title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第三十 袁淑 Volume 70 Biographies 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十 袁淑

translations.literal: Biographies 30: Yuan Shu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 30: Yuan Shu

sentences.zh: 袁淑，字陽源，陳郡陽夏人，丹陽尹豹少子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, style name Yangyuan, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery and the youngest son of Bao, Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, styled Yangyuan, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and was the youngest son of Danyang Governor Bao.

sentences.zh: 少有風氣，年數歲，伯湛謂家人曰：「此非凡兒。

translations.literal: From youth he had spirit and bearing; when only a few years old, his elder uncle Zhan said to the family: "This is no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a small child he showed spirit; his uncle Zhan told the household, "This is no ordinary boy.

sentences.zh: 」至十餘歲，為姑夫王弘所賞。

translations.literal: " By his teens he won the admiration of his uncle-by-marriage Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: " By his teens he had won the admiration of his uncle-by-marriage Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 不為章句之學，而博涉多通，好屬文，辭采遒豔，縱橫有才辯。

translations.literal: He did not pursue exegetical studies but ranged broadly and mastered many fields; he loved composing literature, his style forceful and brilliant, and he was gifted in eloquent disputation.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped narrow exegetical study yet ranged widely across learning; he loved to write, in a forceful and brilliant style, and debated with eloquent skill.

sentences.zh: 本州命主簿，著作佐郎，太子舍人，並不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him chief clerk, and he was offered the posts of Assistant in the Writing Office and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: The province made him chief clerk and offered him posts as assistant in the writing office and attendant of the heir apparent, but he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康命為軍司祭酒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng Yikang appointed him Libationer of the Army Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang appointed him libationer of the army staff.

sentences.zh: 義康不好文學，雖外相禮接，意好甚疏。

translations.literal: Yikang did not care for literature; though he treated Shu with outward courtesy, in his heart he was quite distant.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang cared little for letters; though he treated Shu with outward courtesy, inwardly he kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 劉湛，淑從母兄也，欲其附己，而淑不以為意，由是大相乖失，以久疾免官。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, Shu's cousin on his mother's side, wanted Shu to attach himself to him, but Shu paid no heed; because of this they fell greatly out, and Shu was dismissed on grounds of long illness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, a maternal cousin, wanted Shu at his side, but Shu would not oblige; they fell out sharply, and Shu was dismissed after a long illness.

sentences.zh: 補衡陽王義季右軍主簿，遷太子洗馬，以腳疾不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right Army to the Prince of Hengyang Yiji, then promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent, but on account of foot ailment he did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right-army chief clerk to Prince of Hengyang Yiji, then promoted to groom of the heir apparent, but a foot ailment kept him from taking office.

sentences.zh: 衛軍臨川王義慶雅好文章，請為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, who greatly loved literature, requested him as Consultation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, a great lover of literature, asked for him as consultation officer.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Western Attendant of the Left in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became western attendant of the left in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出為宣城太守，入補中書侍郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, then entered the capital as Gentleman of the Secretariat, and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrator of Xuancheng, returned as gentleman of the secretariat, and left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became palace aide to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia he was made gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 其秋，大舉北伐，淑侍坐從容曰：「今當鳴鑾中嶽，席捲趙、魏，檢玉岱宗，今其時也。

translations.literal: That autumn, when a great northern campaign was launched, Shu sat in attendance and said calmly: "Now is the time to sound the imperial bells at Mount Song, sweep through Zhao and Wei, and inspect the jade at Mount Dai.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, as a great northern campaign was launched, Shu said calmly at court: "Now is the time to ring the bells at Mount Song, sweep Zhao and Wei, and inspect the jade at Mount Dai.

sentences.zh: 臣逢千載之會，願上《封禪書》一篇。

translations.literal: Your servant meets an age that comes once in a thousand years and wishes to present a piece on the feng and shan rites."
translations.idiomatic: I meet an age that comes once in a millennium and wish to present a treatise on the feng and shan rites."

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「盛德之事，我何足以當之。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor laughed and said: "A deed of supreme virtue—how could I be worthy of it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen laughed and said, "A deed of supreme virtue—how could I be worthy of that?"

sentences.zh: 」出為始興王征北長史、南東海太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the North to the Prince of Shixing and Administrator of Eastern Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk of the pacification of the north to Prince of Shixing and administrator of Eastern Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 淑始到府，浚引見，謂曰：「不意舅遂垂屈佐。

translations.literal: When Shu first arrived at the prince's residence, Jun summoned him and said: "I did not expect my uncle to stoop to serve as aide."
translations.idiomatic: When Shu first arrived, Jun received him and said, "I never expected my uncle to condescend to serve as my aide."

sentences.zh: 」淑答曰：「朝廷遣下官，本以光公府望。

translations.literal: Shu replied: "The court sent me down precisely to lend luster to your princely house."
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "The court sent me precisely to lend luster to your princely house."

sentences.zh: 」還為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital as Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as director of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時索虜南侵，遂至瓜步，太祖使百官議防禦之術，淑上議曰：

translations.literal: At that time the northern enemy invaded the south as far as Guabu; the Taizu Emperor had all officials discuss methods of defense, and Shu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy pushed south as far as Guabu; Emperor Wen had officials debate defense, and Shu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞函車之獸，離山必斃；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that beasts that travel in covered carts perish once they leave the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that beasts carried in covered carts die once they leave the mountains;

sentences.zh: 絕波之鱗，宕流則枯。

translations.literal: fish that ride the waves wither when the current fails.
translations.idiomatic: fish that ride the waves wither when the current fails.

sentences.zh: 羯寇遺醜，趨致畿甸，蟻萃螽集，聞已崩殪。

translations.literal: The remnant ugliness of the Jie bandits has rushed to the capital region; like ants and locusts they swarm—word is they are already collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jie remnant has rushed to the capital region; swarming like ants and locusts, they are said already to be collapsing.

sentences.zh: 天險岩曠，地限深遐，故全魏戢其圖，盛晉輟其議，情屈力殫，氣挫勇竭，諒不虞於來臨，本無怵於能濟矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's barriers are lofty and wide, earth's limits deep and far—thus all Wei folded its designs, great Jin stayed its plans; their will bent and strength spent, spirit broken and courage exhausted; they did not expect our coming and had no fear we could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's barriers are vast, earth's limits remote—so Wei folded its plans and Jin stayed its hand; will bent, strength spent, spirit broken, courage exhausted; they never expected our coming and never feared we could prevail.

sentences.zh: 乃者燮定攜遠，阻違授律，由將有弛拙，故士少鬥志。

translations.literal: Yet lately, in settling the distant and carrying the far, we blocked and violated the laws of war—because the generals grew lax and clumsy, the troops lost heart to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, in pacifying the distant, we blocked and violated the laws of war—the generals grew lax, the troops lost heart.

sentences.zh: 圍潰之眾，匪寇傾淪，攻制之師，空自班散，濟西勁騎，急戰蹴旅，淮上訓卒，簡備靡旗。

translations.literal: The surrounded masses were not overthrown by the enemy; the attacking armies scattered of themselves; the strong cavalry of western Ji fought in haste and trampled their own ranks; the drilled soldiers of the Huai were lightly equipped and lost their banners.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged masses were not crushed by the foe; attacking armies scattered on their own; Ji's strong cavalry fought in haste and trampled their ranks; Huai trainees were lightly armed and lost their banners.

sentences.zh: 是由綏整寡衷，戎昭多昧，遂使栲潞入患，泉伊來擾，紛殄姬風，泯毒禹績，騰書有渭陰之迫，懸烽均咸陽之警。

translations.literal: Hence the command was poorly harmonized and military discipline dim; thus Gaolu brought disaster and Quanyi came to harass; the Ji wind was scattered, Yu's traces poisoned; urgent dispatches pressed the north of the Wei, beacon fires matched the alarm at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Command was poorly harmonized, military discipline dim; Gaolu brought disaster, Quanyi harassed; Ji customs scattered, Yu's legacy poisoned; dispatches pressed Wei's north, beacons matched Xianyang's alarm.

sentences.zh: 然而切揣虛實，伏匿先彰，校索伎能，譎詭既顯。

translations.literal: Yet probing emptiness and substance, their hiding was revealed beforehand; testing skills and arts, their deceits were already exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet probing substance and void, their hiding was revealed; testing skill, their deceits were exposed.

sentences.zh: 綿地千里，彌行阻深，表裏躓硋，後先介逼。

translations.literal: A thousand li of land, yet their march is blocked and deep; inside and outside they stumble, advance and rear press upon each other.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li of territory, yet march is blocked and deep; inside and outside they stumble, front and rear press tight.

sentences.zh: 舍陵衍之習，競湍沙之利。

translations.literal: They abandon the habit of level hills and compete for the advantage of rushing sands.
translations.idiomatic: They abandon level hills and compete for rushing sands.

sentences.zh: 今虹見萍生，土膏泉動，津陸陷溢，痁禍洊興，芻稿已單，米粟莫系，水宇衿帶，進必傾殞，河隘扁固，退亦墮滅。

translations.literal: Now rainbows appear and duckweed sprouts, clay oozes and springs stir, fords and roads flood, malarial plague rises again, fodder is gone, grain cannot be tied—water belts the land, advance must topple and perish, rivers narrow and dikes firm, retreat also falls to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Now rainbows appear, duckweed sprouts, clay oozes, springs stir; fords flood, plague returns; fodder gone, grain untied—waters belt the land: advance means ruin, rivers narrow: retreat means doom.

sentences.zh: 所謂棲烏於烈火之上，養魚于叢棘之中。

translations.literal: This is what is called nesting birds over blazing fire and raising fish amid thorn thickets.
translations.idiomatic: This is nesting birds over fire and raising fish in thorns.

sentences.zh: 或謂損緩江右，寬繕淮內。

translations.literal: Some say we should ease the right bank of the Yang and relax defenses within the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Some say ease the Yang's right bank and relax Huai defenses.

sentences.zh: 竊謂拯扼閩城，舊史為允，棄遠涼士，前言稱非。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that to save Min city is approved in old histories, but to abandon the distant cool lands is called wrong in earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that saving Min city is approved in old histories, but abandoning distant borderlands was called wrong before.

sentences.zh: 限此要荒，猶弗委割。

translations.literal: Even for this remote frontier they would not cast it away.
translations.idiomatic: Even that remote frontier they would not cast away.

sentences.zh: 況聯被京國，咫尺神甸，數州摧掃，列邑殲痍，山淵反覆，草木塗地。

translations.literal: How much more when the capital is linked and the sacred domain is within a stone's throw—several provinces swept bare, cities destroyed, mountains and rivers overturned, grass and trees painted with corpses.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the capital lies linked, the sacred domain within reach—provinces swept bare, cities ruined, land overturned, grass and trees painted with dead.

sentences.zh: 今丘賦千乘，井算萬集，肩摩倍于長安，締袂百於臨淄，什一而籍，實慊氓願，履畝以稅，既協農和。

translations.literal: Now the hill tax fields a thousand chariots, wells reckon ten thousand gatherings; shoulders rub more than in Chang'an, sleeves tighten more than in Linzi; a one-in-ten levy truly answers the people's wish, taxing by the mu already suits farming harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Now hill taxes field a thousand chariots, wells reckon ten thousand households; shoulders crowd beyond Chang'an, sleeves press beyond Linzi; one-tenth levies answer the people, mu taxation suits the harvest.

sentences.zh: 戶競戰心，人含銳志，皆欲贏糧請奮，釋緯乘城。

translations.literal: Households compete in war spirit; men hold sharp resolve—all wish to carry extra grain and beg to strike, cast off weaving and mount the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Households compete in war spirit; men hold sharp resolve—all wish to carry grain and fight, cast off looms and man the walls.

sentences.zh: 謂宜懸金鑄印，要壯果之士，重幣甘辭，招摧決之將，舉薦板築之下，抽登臺皁之間，賞之以焚書，報之以相爵，俄而昭才賀闕，異能間至。

translations.literal: It is fitting to hang gold and cast seals, summon men of fierce courage; offer heavy gifts and sweet words, recruit men resolved to break the foe; draw from below the foundation platforms and pull from among the black-clad clerks; reward them with the burning of books and repay them with ministerial rank—soon outstanding talent will fill the gate and unusual ability arrive in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Hang gold and cast seals for fierce men; heavy gifts and sweet words for the resolute; draw talent from the lowly and the clerks; reward with burned books, repay with rank—soon talent and skill will arrive.

sentences.zh: 戎貪而無謀，肆而不整，迷乎向背之次，謬於合散之宜，犯軍志之極害，觸兵家之甚諱。

translations.literal: The enemy is greedy without plan, rampant without order, lost in the sequence of advance and retreat, mistaken in the fit of gathering and scattering, touching the army's utmost harm and the strategist's greatest taboo.
translations.idiomatic: They are greedy without plan, rampant without order, lost in advance and retreat, wrong in gathering and scattering, touching the army's worst harm and the strategist's greatest taboo.

sentences.zh: 鹹畜憤矣，僉策戰矣，稱願影從，謠言緡命。

translations.literal: All store up anger; all draw up battle plans; they call out to follow in shadow and rumor binds their lives.
translations.idiomatic: All store anger; all draw battle plans; they beg to follow, rumor binds their lives.

sentences.zh: 宜選敢悍數千，騖行潛掩，偃旗裹甲，鉗馬銜枚，檜稽而起，晨壓未陣，旌噪亂舉，火鼓四臨，使景不暇移，塵不及起，無不禽鎩獸讋，冰解霧散，掃洗哨類，漂鹵浮山。

translations.literal: It is fitting to choose several thousand daring men, ride swiftly and strike in secret, lower banners and wrap armor, muzzle horses and gag mouths, rise like the cypress pestle at dawn and press the camp before it forms; banners shout and chaos rises, fire drums close from four sides—so they cannot shift their gaze or lift the dust; none will not be seized and beasts tremble, ice melts and mist scatters, scouts swept away, captives float like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Choose thousands of daring men, ride swift and strike hidden, lower banners, wrap armor, muzzle horses, gag mouths; rise at dawn and press the unformed camp; chaos, fire, drums on four sides—they cannot move; all will be seized, ice melt, scouts swept, captives heaped like mountains.

sentences.zh: 如有決罦漏網，逡窠逗穴，命淮、汝戈船，遏其還徑，兗部勁卒，梗其歸塗。

translations.literal: If any break the net or linger in holes, order the Huai and Ru oar-boats to block their return, and Yan's crack troops to choke their homeward road.
translations.idiomatic: If any escape the net, order Huai and Ru boats to block return and Yan's crack troops to choke the homeward road.

sentences.zh: 必剪元雄，懸首麾下，乃將只輪不反，戰轊無旋矣。

translations.literal: Surely the chief enemy will be cut down and his head hung beneath the banners; then not even a wheel will return, not even a wheel-hub of the army will turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the chief will be cut down, head hung beneath the banners; not a wheel will return.

sentences.zh: 於是信臣騰威，武士繕力，緹組接陰，鞞柝聯響。

translations.literal: Then loyal ministers will soar in might, warriors will trim their strength, patrol cords will link in shade, watch-rattles will sound in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Then loyal ministers rise in might, warriors sharpen strength, patrol cords link, watch-rattles sound in turn.

sentences.zh: 若其偽遁羸張，出沒無際，楚言漢旆，顯默如神，固已日月蔽虧，川穀蕩貿。

translations.literal: If they feign retreat and feign strength, appearing and vanishing without bound, with Chu speech and Han banners, manifest and hidden like spirits—already sun and moon are eclipsed and valleys overturned.
translations.idiomatic: If they feign retreat, appear and vanish without bound, Chu speech and Han banners, manifest and hidden like spirits—sun and moon eclipsed, valleys overturned.

sentences.zh: 負塞殘孽，阻山燼黨，收險竊命，憑城借土，則當因威席捲，乘機芟剿。

translations.literal: Those remnant villains who hold passes and cling to hills, gathering danger and stealing life, relying on walls and native earth—then we should roll up power like a mat and seize the moment to cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants holding passes and hills, stealing life behind walls—then roll up power and cut them down at once.

sentences.zh: 泗、汴秀士，星流電燭，徐、阜嚴兵，雨湊雲集，蹶亂桑溪之北，搖潰浣海以南，絕其心根，勿使能植，銜索之枯，幾何不蠹。

translations.literal: The fine men of Si and Bian stream like stars and flash like lightning; Yan and Fu's stern troops gather like rain and clouds; trample disorder north of Sangxi, shake collapse south of Huanghai; cut their root so they cannot plant again—the bound dry tree, how can it not rot?
translations.idiomatic: Si and Bian's fine men stream like stars; Xu and Fu's troops gather like clouds; trample north of Sangxi, shake south of Huanghai; cut the root so nothing grows—the bound dry tree cannot fail to rot.

sentences.zh: 是由涸澤而漁，焚林而狩，若浚風之亻舞輕籜，杲日之拂浮霜。

translations.literal: Thus draining the marsh to fish and burning the forest to hunt—like a keen wind shaking light bamboo, like bright sun brushing floating frost.
translations.idiomatic: Thus drain the marsh to fish, burn the forest to hunt—like keen wind on bamboo, like bright sun on frost.

sentences.zh: 既而尉洽荷掠之餘，望吊網悲之鬼。

translations.literal: Then comfort those left from the sweep of the net and gaze down to comfort the ghosts caught in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Then comfort those left from the net's sweep and mourn the ghosts caught in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 然後天行樞運，猋舉煙升，青蓋西巡，翠華東幸，經啟州野，滌一軫策，俾高闕再勒，燕然後銘。

translations.literal: Then heaven's pivot will turn, whirlwinds rise and smoke ascends; the green canopy tours west, the emerald banner visits east; the provinces are opened and wild lands cleansed with a single rein-turn, so the high tower is carved again and Yanran inscribed afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Then heaven's pivot turns, whirlwinds rise; the green canopy tours west, emerald banner east; provinces opened, wild lands cleansed at one rein-turn—the high tower carved again, Yanran inscribed after.

sentences.zh: 方乃奠山沉河，創禮輯策，闡耀炎、昊之遺則，貫軼商、夏之舊文。

translations.literal: Then mountains will be laid, rivers sunk, ritual created and registers compiled, blazing the legacy of Yan and Hao, threading through the old texts of Shang and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Then mountains laid, rivers sunk, ritual made, registers compiled, blazing Yan and Hao's legacy, threading Shang and Xia's old texts.

sentences.zh: 今眾賈拳勇，而將術疏怯，意者稔泰日積，承平歲久，邑無驚赴之急，家緩饋戰之勤，闕閱訓之禮，簡參屬之飾，且亦薦采之法，庸未蔇歟。

translations.literal: Now the masses are brave in fist but generals' arts are sparse and timid—the thought is that long peace has piled up, years of ease are many, towns have no alarm of rushing to battle, homes lack the toil of feeding war, the rites of review and drill are wanting, the adornment of mustering subordinates is thin, and perhaps the method of recommending talent has not yet ripened.
translations.idiomatic: Now the masses are brave but generals timid—long peace piled high, ease for years; towns lack alarm, homes lack war toil, drill rites wanting, muster adornment thin, and recommending talent may not yet have ripened.

sentences.zh: 若乃邦造裏選，攉論深切，躬擐盡幽，斬帶尋遠，設有沉明能照，俊偉自宣，誠感泉雨，流通金石，氣懾飛、賁，知窮苴、起，審邪正順逆之數，達昏明益損之宜，能睽合民心，愚睿物性，登丹墀而敷策，躡青蒲而揚謀，上說辰鑒，下弭素言，足以安民紓國，救災恤患。

translations.literal: If the state chooses from districts and lanes, plucks discourse deep and cutting, personally bears the utmost secrets and traces the far with the sword-belt—suppose there is one whose clarity shines, whose excellence declares itself, whose sincerity moves spring rain and flows through metal and stone, whose spirit awes Fei and Ben, whose knowledge exhausts Ju and Qi, who judges the numbers of evil and straight, fortune and loss, who can harmonize the people's hearts and know the nature of dull and keen—ascending the cinnabar steps to lay out plans, treading the green rush to raise counsel, persuading the imperial mirror above and quieting plain words below—such a one could settle the people, ease the state, save disaster and pity the afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: If the state chooses deeply from districts, bears utmost secrets, traces the far—one whose clarity shines, excellence declares itself, sincerity moves rain, spirit awes heroes, knowledge exhausts sages, judges fortune and loss, harmonizes hearts, knows dull and keen, lays plans on cinnabar steps, raises counsel on green rush, persuades the throne and quiets plain speech—he could settle the people and save disaster.

sentences.zh: 則宜拔過寵貴之上，褒升戚舊之右，別其旂章，榮其班祿，出得專譽，使不稟命。

translations.literal: Then he should be pulled above the over-favored and raised above the kin of honor, given distinct banners and glorious stipend ranks, going out with sole praise and not receiving orders.
translations.idiomatic: Then pull him above the over-favored, raise him above honored kin, give distinct banners and glorious stipends, going out with sole praise without awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 降席折節，同廣武之請；

translations.literal: Lower his mat and bend his knee, as Guangwu requested;
translations.idiomatic: Lower the mat and bend the knee, as Guangwu requested;

sentences.zh: 設壇致禮，均淮陰之授。

translations.literal: set up the altar and grant rites, as Huaiyin was invested.
translations.idiomatic: set up the altar and grant rites, as Huaiyin was invested.

sentences.zh: 必有要盟之功，竊符之捷。

translations.literal: Surely there will be the merit of sworn alliance and the swiftness of stealing the tally.
translations.idiomatic: Surely there will be sworn alliance's merit and stealing the tally's swiftness.

sentences.zh: 夷裔暴狠，內外侮棄，始附之眾，分茷無序，蠱以威利，勢必攜離，首順之徒，靡然自及。

translations.literal: Barbarians are violent and cruel, inner and outer scorn them; those who first attach are split and without order—bewitch them with might and profit and they will surely fall apart; those who lead in submission will crumble of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians are violent; inner and outer scorn them; first attachments split without order—bewitch with might and profit and they fall apart; leaders in submission crumble themselves.

sentences.zh: 今淶繹故典，瀍土纓緌，翦焉幽播，折首凶狡。

translations.literal: Now the old canons are glossed, the land sprinkled with tassels, the hidden scattered, the fierce heads cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Now old canons are glossed, land sprinkled with tassels, the hidden scattered, fierce heads cut down.

sentences.zh: 是猶眇者願明，痿之思步，動商遄會，功終易感。

translations.literal: This is like the dim wishing for brightness, the lame wishing to walk—move and the meeting comes swift, the work ends and feeling follows.
translations.idiomatic: This is the dim wishing for light, the lame wishing to walk—move and the meeting comes swift, work ends and feeling follows.

sentences.zh: 劫晉在於善覘，全鄭實寄良諜，多縱反間，汨惑心耳，發險易之前，抵興喪之術，沖其猜伏，拂其嫌嗜，汨以連率之貴，餌以析壤之資。

translations.literal: Seizing Jin lay in keen sight; preserving Zheng truly rested on good spies—use many counter-schemes, muddy and confuse their ears, send before the steep and easy, strike the art of rise and fall, probe their suspicions, brush their dislikes, muddy them with the honor of joint command, bait them with the asset of carved lands.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing Jin lay in keen sight; preserving Zheng in good spies—use counter-schemes, muddy their ears, strike rise and fall, probe suspicion, brush dislike, muddy with joint command, bait with carved lands.

sentences.zh: 罄筆端之用，展辭鋒之銳，振辯則堅圍可解，馳羽而岩邑易傾。

translations.literal: Exhaust the brush's use, unfold the rhetorical blade's edge—shake debate and stout walls open, send a feather and stony towns lean.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the brush, unfold rhetoric's edge—debate shakes stout walls, a feather leans stony towns.

sentences.zh: 必府鬲土崩，枝幹瓦裂，故燕、樂相悔，項、範交疑矣。

translations.literal: Surely the storehouse will collapse, branches and trunk split like tiles—thus Yan and Yue regretted each other, Xiang and Fan grew mutual doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the storehouse collapses, trunk splits like tile—Yan and Yue regret each other, Xiang and Fan grow doubt.

sentences.zh: 或乃言約功深，事邇應廣，齊圉反駕，趙養還君，盡輿誦之道，畢能事之效。

translations.literal: Or words few and merit deep, affairs near yet response wide—Qi lord returned his carriage, Zhao lord restored his lord, all the ways of cart and recitation, the full effect of able service.
translations.idiomatic: Or few words, deep merit, near affairs, wide response—Qi lord returned carriage, Zhao lord restored lord, all cart and recitation's ways, full able service.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得出內層禁，遊心明代，澤與身泰，恩隨年行，無以逢迎昌運，潤飾鴻法。

translations.literal: Your servant has been fortunate to leave the inner forbidden, wander heart in the bright age, grace equal to body, favor following years, yet has nothing with which to meet the flourishing fortune and adorn the great law.
translations.idiomatic: I have been fortunate to leave the inner forbidden, wander heart in this bright age, grace with body, favor with years, yet have nothing to meet flourishing fortune and adorn great law.

sentences.zh: 今塗有遺鏃，蠆未息蜂，敢思涼識，少酬閎施。

translations.literal: Now on the road lie spent arrows; the scorpion's sting has not ceased—dare I think cool thoughts and slightly repay the broad bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: Now spent arrows lie on the road; the scorpion's sting has not ceased—I dare think cool thoughts and slightly repay broad grace.

sentences.zh: 但坐幕既乏昭文，免胄不能致果，竊觀都護之邊論，屬國之兵謨，終、晁之抗辭，杜、耿之言事，咸云及經之棘，猶闕上算，燭郛之敬，裁收下策。

translations.literal: Yet the seat of command lacks brilliance in writing; without helmet one cannot achieve the result—your servant has seen the frontier discussions of the Protector-General, the military plans of the Commandant for Dependencies, the resisting words of Zhong and Chao, the policy speeches of Du and Geng—all say that even the thorns of the classics still lack the highest calculation, and the respect of beacon towers only barely reaches the lower strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet command lacks brilliance; without helmet no result—I have seen frontier discussions, dependency plans, Zhong and Chao's words, Du and Geng's policy—all say classics' thorns still lack highest calculation, beacon respect barely reaches lower strategy.

sentences.zh: 自恥懦木，智不綜微，敢露昧見，無會昭采。

translations.literal: Ashamed of my timid wood, my wisdom does not gather the subtle—I dare reveal dull views, without meeting bright selection.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of timid wood, wisdom not gathering subtlety—I dare reveal dull views, without meeting bright selection.

sentences.zh: 淑喜為誇誕，每為時人所嘲。

translations.literal: Shu delighted in grand exaggeration and was often mocked by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Shu loved grand exaggeration and was often mocked by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗送錢三萬餉淑，一宿複遣追取，謂使人謬誤，欲以戲淑。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Jun once sent thirty thousand cash to present to Shu; after one night he sent again to recover it, telling the messenger it was a mistake and intending to tease Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Jun once sent thirty thousand cash to Shu; after one night he sent to recover it, claiming a messenger's error, intending to tease him.

sentences.zh: 淑與浚書曰：「袁司直之視館，敢寓書于上國之宮尹。

translations.literal: Shu wrote to Jun: "Director Yuan of the Secretariat ventures to lodge a letter with the palace steward of the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wrote to Jun: "Director Yuan ventures to lodge a letter with the upper state's palace steward.

sentences.zh: 日者猥枉泉賦，降委弊邑。

translations.literal: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy, lowering it upon my poor district.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you wrongly sent a spring levy upon my poor district.

sentences.zh: 弊邑敬事是遑，無或違貳。

translations.literal: My poor district respectfully attends to the matter and dares not be double-minded.
translations.idiomatic: My district respectfully attends and dares not be double-minded.

sentences.zh: 懼非郊贈之禮，覲饗之資，不虞君王惠之於是也，是有懵焉。

translations.literal: I fear it is not the gift for suburban presentation or the resource for court audience, and did not expect the king's grace upon it—therefore there is confusion.
translations.idiomatic: I fear it is not suburban gift or audience resource, and did not expect the king's grace—therefore confusion.

sentences.zh: 弗圖旦夕發咫尺之記，籍左右而請，以為胥授失旨，爰速先幣。

translations.literal: I did not think that within the day a note of a foot's nearness would arrive, and through your attendants you would request it back, thinking the relay had missed the mark and hastening the first gift.
translations.idiomatic: I did not think that within the day a note would arrive through your attendants to take it back, thinking relay error and hastening the first gift.

sentences.zh: 曾是附庸臣委末學孤聞者，如之何勿疑。

translations.literal: How could a dependent minister like me, of meager learning and lonely hearing, not doubt?
translations.idiomatic: How could a dependent minister of meager learning not doubt?

sentences.zh: 且亦聞之前志曰，七年之中，一與一奪，義士猶或非之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard in former records that within seven years, one giving and one taking—even a man of righteousness might fault it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover former records say that within seven years one giving and one taking—even a righteous man might fault it.

sentences.zh: 況密邇旬次，何其裒益之亟也。

translations.literal: How much more when it is close within a ten-day span—how sudden this repeated gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: How much more within a ten-day span—how sudden this gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 藉恐二三諸侯，有以觀大國之政。

translations.literal: I fear the several feudal lords may use this to observe the great state's government.
translations.idiomatic: I fear feudal lords may observe the great state's government through this.

sentences.zh: 是用敢布心腹。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare lay bare my inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I dare lay bare my heart.

sentences.zh: 弊室弱生，砥節清廉，好是潔直，以不邪之故，而貧聞天下。

translations.literal: My poor house and weak life polish integrity and keep purity; I love straightforwardness and, because I am not crooked, am poor and known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: My poor house polishes integrity; I love straightness and, because I am not crooked, am known poor throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 甯有昧夫嗟金者哉。

translations.literal: Would there be one blind to sigh over gold?
translations.idiomatic: Would anyone blind sigh over gold?

sentences.zh: 不腆供賦，束馬先璧以俟命。

translations.literal: With meager tribute I bind the horses and send the jade first to await your command.
translations.idiomatic: With meager tribute I bind horses and send jade first to await command.

sentences.zh: 唯執事所以圖之。」

translations.literal: Only the steward may decide."
translations.idiomatic: Only the steward may decide."

sentences.zh: 遷太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the left guard of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元兇將為弑逆，其夜淑在直，二更許，呼淑及蕭斌等流涕謂曰：「主上信讒，將見罪廢。

translations.literal: When the Traitor Prince was about to commit regicide, that night Shu was on duty; about the second watch Shao called Shu and Xiao Bin and others, weeping as he told them: "The emperor trusts slander; I am about to be charged and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Traitor Prince was about to commit regicide, Shu was on duty that night; about the second watch Shao called Shu and Xiao Bin, weeping: "The emperor trusts slander; I am about to be charged and deposed.

sentences.zh: 內省無過，不能受枉。

translations.literal: Looking within, I have no fault and cannot accept injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Looking within I have no fault and cannot accept injustice.

sentences.zh: 明旦便當行大事，望相與戮力。

translations.literal: Tomorrow I must carry out a great affair; I hope you will strive together with me.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I must act; I hope you will strive with me.

sentences.zh: 」淑及斌並曰：「自古無此，願加善思。

translations.literal: Shu and Bin both said: "Since antiquity there has never been this; please think more carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Bin both said, "Since antiquity there has never been this; please think again."

sentences.zh: 」劭怒變色，左右皆動。

translations.literal: Shao's face changed in anger and those around him all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's face changed in anger; those around stirred.

sentences.zh: 斌懼，乃曰：「臣昔忝伏事，常思效節，況憂迫如此，輒當竭身奉令。

translations.literal: Bin in fear then said: "Your servant once served at your side and always thought to repay with loyalty; now that distress presses so, I will exhaust myself to obey."
translations.idiomatic: Bin in fear said, "I once served you and thought to repay with loyalty; pressed so, I will obey."

sentences.zh: 」淑叱之曰：「卿便謂殿下真有是邪？

translations.literal: Shu rebuked him: "Do you really think His Highness truly intends this?
translations.idiomatic: Shu rebuked him, "Do you think His Highness truly intends this?

sentences.zh: 殿下幼時嘗患風，或是疾動耳。

translations.literal: His Highness in youth once suffered wind ailment; perhaps this is only the illness stirring."
translations.idiomatic: His Highness in youth suffered wind ailment; perhaps the illness stirs again."

sentences.zh: 」劭愈怒，因問曰：「事當克不？

translations.literal: Shao grew still angrier and therefore asked: "Will the affair succeed or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Shao grew angrier and asked, "Will it succeed or not?

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「居不疑之地，何患不克。

translations.literal: Shu said: "In a position without doubt, why fear failure?
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "In a position without doubt, why fear failure?

sentences.zh: 但既克之後，為天地之所不容，大禍亦旋至耳。

translations.literal: But once you succeed, heaven and earth will not contain you; great disaster will swiftly arrive as well.
translations.idiomatic: But once you succeed, heaven and earth will not contain you; great disaster will swiftly come.

sentences.zh: 願急息之。

translations.literal: I beg you to stop it quickly."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to stop at once."

sentences.zh: 」劭左右引淑等袴褶，又就主衣取錦，截三尺為一段，又中破，分斌、淑及左右，使以縛袴。

translations.literal: Shao's attendants pulled Shu and the others by their trousers; they also went to the imperial wardrobe for brocade, cut three feet per section, then cut those in half, and divided them among Bin, Shu, and the attendants to bind their trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's men pulled their trousers; took brocade from the wardrobe, cut three-foot sections, halved them, and divided them to bind Bin, Shu, and attendants.

sentences.zh: 淑出環省，繞床行，至四更乃寢。

translations.literal: Shu went out and walked around the hall, circling the bed; only at the fourth watch did he sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Shu went out, walked around the hall circling the bed, and slept only at the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 劭將出，已與蕭斌同載，呼淑甚急，淑眠終不起。

translations.literal: When Shao was about to go out, he was already in the same carriage as Xiao Bin and called urgently for Shu; Shu slept to the end and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao was about to go out with Xiao Bin, he called urgently for Shu; Shu slept on and did not rise.

sentences.zh: 劭停車奉化門，催之相續。

translations.literal: Shao stopped the carriage at Fenghua Gate and urged him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shao stopped at Fenghua Gate and urged him again and again.

sentences.zh: 徐起至車後，劭使登車，又辭不上。

translations.literal: Shu slowly rose and came behind the carriage; Shao ordered him to mount, and again he declined and would not get on.
translations.idiomatic: Shu slowly came behind the carriage; Shao ordered him up, and again he refused.

sentences.zh: 劭因命左右：「與手刃。

translations.literal: Shao therefore ordered those around him: "Give him a blade in hand."
translations.idiomatic: Shao ordered those around him, "Cut him down."

sentences.zh: 」見殺於奉化門外，時年四十六。

translations.literal: He was killed outside Fenghua Gate, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed outside Fenghua Gate at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 劭即位，追贈太常，賜賵甚厚。

translations.literal: When Shao took the throne he posthumously honored him as Director of Ceremonies and gave lavish funeral goods.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao took the throne he posthumously made him director of ceremonies with lavish funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 子幾、敳、棱、凝、標。

translations.literal: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ji, Ai, Leng, Ning, and Biao.

sentences.zh: 敳，世祖步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Ai was Commandant of the Footsoldiers under the Shizu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was commandant of the footsoldiers under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 凝，太宗世禦史中丞，出為晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Ning was Director of the Censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was director of the censorate under the Taizong Emperor and went out as administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 太宗初與四方同反，兵敗歸降，以補劉湛冠軍府主簿。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Taizong Emperor he rebelled with the four quarters; when his army was defeated he returned and surrendered, and was appointed chief clerk in Liu Zhan's army of the champion general.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's first year he rebelled with the four quarters; defeated, he surrendered and was made chief clerk in Liu Zhan's champion army.

sentences.zh: 淑諸子並早卒。

translations.literal: All Shu's sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: All Shu's sons died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天長地久，人道則異於斯。

translations.literal: The historian says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, yet the human way differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Heaven is long and earth enduring, yet the human way differs.

sentences.zh: 蕣華朝露，未足以言也。

translations.literal: Hibiscus at morning dew is not enough to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Hibiscus in morning dew is not enough to speak of.

sentences.zh: 其間夭遽，曾何足雲。

translations.literal: Among them, sudden early death—how can it be worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: Sudden early death among them—how can it be worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 宜任心去留，不以存沒嬰心。

translations.literal: One should let the heart go or stay and not let life and death trouble the mind.
translations.idiomatic: Let the heart go or stay; do not let life and death trouble the mind.

sentences.zh: 徒以靈化悠遠，生不再來，雖天行路險，而未之斯遇，謂七尺常存，百年可保也。

translations.literal: Only because spirit's transformation is far and distant and life does not come twice, though heaven's road is perilous one has not yet met it, one thinks the seven feet will always remain and a hundred years can be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Because spirit is far and life does not return, though heaven's road is perilous one has not met it, one thinks the body will always remain and a hundred years can be kept.

sentences.zh: 所以據洪圖而輕天下，吝寸陰而敗尺璧。

translations.literal: Therefore one holds the great design and treats the realm lightly, grudges an inch of shadow and loses a foot of jade.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one holds great design lightly, grudges an inch of shadow and loses a foot of jade.

sentences.zh: 若乃義重乎生，空炳前誥，投軀殉主，世罕其人。

translations.literal: If righteousness outweighs life, it shines alone in former edicts; to cast away the body and die for one's lord is rare in the world.
translations.idiomatic: If righteousness outweighs life, it shines in former edicts; to die for one's lord is rare in the world.

sentences.zh: 若無陽源之節，丹青何貴焉爾！

translations.literal: Without Yangyuan's integrity, how would the vermillion and green be prized!
translations.idiomatic: Without Yangyuan's integrity, how would vermillion and green be prized!
